audits.title: Recognition session event contract, payload conversion, and minimum recording gate
notes: Recognition event reduction matches upstream: any Error event fails, the last FinalText wins, and Completed without Final/Error is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend failure.

Empty recognition returns an empty recognition payload, skips scene text postprocessing, and follows recording -> inferring -> idle without a postprocessing status; private D-Bus coverage proves the method reply and RecognitionResult carry the same empty payload.

Restored the upstream 8000 raw-sample minimum: shorter recordings cancel the session, return directly to idle, skip ASR/text finishing, and expose an exact empty StopRecording D-Bus reply without RecognitionResult.

Aligned streaming text projection so non-empty PartialText and early FinalText are emitted through RecognitionPartial during recording while early finals remain retained for stop-time payload construction and are not duplicated at stop.

Rust keeps a smaller typed BackendCapabilities shape because current upstream runtime decisions read only audio_delivery_mode; upstream supports_streaming, supports_partial_results, and requires_network are descriptor metadata without runtime consumers, while hotword capability is carried by model/provider metadata in both implementations.

The separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit now owns and implements frozen live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification; this recognition-contract unit remains non-overlapping and only owns event reduction/payload semantics.

audits.title: Recognition result JSON wire format and candidate source interpretation
notes: Daemon-produced raw/llm/asr recognition JSON, invalid-input fallback, commit-text normalization, and raw-candidate synthesis match the frozen upstream wire behavior.
Rust intentionally uses a typed CandidateSource: missing or unknown foreign source strings normalize to raw instead of preserving an arbitrary string; ordinary daemon-produced sources are unaffected.

Rust additionally preserves an empty cancel candidate and exposes RecognitionPayload::cancelled for typed frontend policy. The current Rust daemon does not produce that sentinel, and the frozen upstream defines kSourceCancel/menu handling but has no recognition-result producer for an empty cancel candidate.

audits.title: Core configuration schema, defaults, normalization, persistence, and validation
notes: Fixed dangling active ASR provider validation when the provider list is empty.
Validated input_gain in the upstream 0.1..10.0 range; Rust intentionally fails closed instead of clamping.
Rust scene provider omission remains an intentional extension because runtime provider resolution supports it.
Malformed/future-schema configs remain intentionally fail-closed.

audits.title: LLM command adapter process metadata and working-directory resolution
notes: Restored upstream args-first, command-second script-directory working-directory inference including ~/ expansion.
Explicit Rust working_dir remains a supported extension.
Fingerprint PID records, process groups, PID-reuse protection, and bounded TERM-to-KILL shutdown remain intentional safety enhancements.

audits.title: Scene/LLM post-processing, payload fallback, context, and OpenAI-compatible transport contract
notes: Aligned scoped vinput XML fallback tags, command fallback ordering, ASCII trimming, raw candidate retention, and recoverable LLM failure payloads.
Transport and prompt-file failures now preserve raw/selected+ASR payloads and emit typed warning notifications.
Context cache read failures are non-fatal like upstream.
OpenAI-compatible text connect attempts use the upstream 5-second maximum while scene timeout still bounds the full request.
Known gap: shutdown does not yet actively cancel an in-flight blocking OpenAI-compatible HTTP request; it waits for the request deadline.

audits.title: Prompt file loading and interpolation
notes: Unknown legacy double-brace placeholders remain verbatim.
Rust single-brace extensions no longer accidentally match double-brace legacy placeholders.

audits.title: Configured ASR backend selection and preparation
notes: Fixed local-provider dispatch to depend on type=local rather than the bundled sherpa-onnx provider id, matching upstream support for arbitrary stable local provider ids created by normal config/GUI flows.

Fixed local model backend selection so vinpst-model.json backend is authoritative exactly like upstream: missing/empty defaults offline, sherpa-offline selects offline, sherpa-streaming selects streaming, and unknown non-empty backend values fail closed; descriptive runtime metadata no longer overrides backend.
Command providers preserve the upstream id suffix rule: ids ending in .streaming use the streaming command backend and other command ids use batch mode.

Vinpst native OpenAI-compatible type=remote and the mock provider are intentional extensions beyond the frozen upstream factory; frozen upstream config variants are Local/Command and its browser remote service is a special command-provider path.

Rust build_active_prepared/prepare_backend consolidates warmup by creating and cancelling one session before swap. The corresponding upstream prepare/swap responsibility lives in recognition_session_manager and remains pending for its own non-overlapping audit.
Concrete model discovery/layout and native Sherpa implementation files are only supporting evidence here and remain pending for their dedicated model/backend audits.
Static configured ASR diagnostics now treat empty active_provider as a normal unselected state with empty last_error instead of reporting NoActiveProvider as a load failure.

audits.title: Sherpa runtime configuration bridge
notes: Frozen AsrConfig is a transient backend-construction DTO rather than a persisted user schema. Vinpst intentionally does not recreate a parallel struct: typed provider/global/VAD config plus installed-model metadata flow directly into the Sherpa runtime plans, eliminating one copy/mapping layer.

Every product-bearing default is already pinned by the owning units: Sherpa thread count defaults to 4, offline model metadata may override it, online keeps 4; VAD defaults are enabled=true, threshold=0.45, min_speech_duration=0.15, min_silence_duration=0.5, speech_pad_ms=300; streaming disables VAD; and provider hotwords are carried into the local runtime with the audited support/override rules.

Frozen language is populated from ModelInfo::RuntimeLanguageHint rather than the global UI/default language. Rust likewise derives language-sensitive recognizer settings from installed-model metadata/runtime language hints under ASR-MODEL-001; request context default_language remains a separate recognition-context field and is not used as a substitute for this DTO member.

The only structural VAD-model member is intentionally different: frozen stores compile-time VINPUT_VAD_MODEL_PATH in this DTO, while Vinpst resolves VINPST_SHERPA_VAD_MODEL, user/system XDG data paths, or a development asset at runtime. ASR-VAD-001 owns and tests that divergence, including the same fail-open-to-untrimmed behavior when the model is absent or unloadable.
This bridge audit claims no new Sherpa model/session/VAD behavior; those implementation files are supporting evidence only and retain ownership under ASR-MODEL-001, ASR-SHERPA-001, and ASR-VAD-001.

audits.title: ASR session preparation, reload, and effective-backend state
notes: Fixed the valid empty active_provider state to match upstream disable semantics: startup and reload clear target/effective runtime ownership without treating the state as a backend-load failure, leave last_error empty, and future recording attempts fail only when a session is requested.

Reloading to an unselected provider while recording preserves the already-created active RecognitionSession but clears the effective backend for future sessions, matching upstream shared-backend session lifetime semantics.
Backend preparation still forces one CreateSession/cancel warmup before publication, matching upstream prepare-before-swap behavior.

Rust intentionally waits for Idle before preparing/applying a configured backend, whereas upstream can prepare/swap while a recording is active. This keeps runtime resource mutation outside busy recording/postprocessing phases.

Rust intentionally uses reload generations: stale prepared backends and stale failures are discarded, so an older request cannot be transiently published after a newer request arrives. Frozen upstream may briefly apply the earlier prepared backend before processing the later request.

Rust intentionally does not use the upstream BuildRuntimeSignature no-op optimization. Explicit reload requests therefore re-prepare even for apparently unchanged identity, which also avoids missing changes such as VAD thresholds/durations that the upstream signature does not include.
Reload success is silent and reload failure emits one notification in both implementations. Rust additionally suppresses stale-generation failure notifications.

Process-level --no-asr remains sticky across config reloads in both implementations. Rust intentionally exposes its disable reason through typed/D-Bus diagnostics; frozen upstream only reports that reason to stderr and leaves snapshot last_error empty.

Frozen upstream session snapshots use ResolvePreferredLocalModel even for non-local active providers, while Rust diagnostics report the active Command/Remote provider model. Exact legacy D-Bus state projection is deferred to the separate common/dbus ASR-state audit because the Rust projection file remains pending.

Upstream explicitly joins its reload thread during Shutdown. Rust owns reload work in Tokio tasks; async workers are cancelled with runtime shutdown while spawn_blocking preparation is waited by Tokio runtime teardown. No detached native preparation is intentionally created.

audits.title: Command ASR batch and streaming process protocols
notes: Fixed the main streaming gap: .streaming command providers now own one long-lived helper process across PushAudio calls instead of buffering all PCM until Finish. Intermediate chunks are sent with commit=false, the final pending chunk uses commit=true, and a finish control line closes input exactly like frozen upstream.

The daemon live poller now actively polls asynchronous streaming sessions on every tick, so helper stdout produced after PushAudio returns can reach RecognitionPartial before StopRecording. Early FinalText remains retained for the final payload and is not duplicated at stop.

Streaming JSON event handling matches upstream for session_started/empty/unknown no-ops, trimmed partial/final/final_timestamps text, duplicate-partial suppression, blank error fallback, closed completion, and malformed JSON fail-closed behavior.

Streaming cancel best-effort starts the helper, sends a cancel control event, emits Completed, and terminates the helper process group; tests prove descendant cleanup. Buffered command cancel now also emits Completed and buffered Finish is idempotent like upstream.

Batch command providers continue to write raw signed-16 little-endian PCM and use trimmed stdout as final text. On supported little-endian Linux targets this matches upstream native i16 byte transport.

Vinpst intentionally retains stronger process safety than frozen upstream: command helpers run in their own process group, direct-child exit cleans descendants, and stdout/stderr are independently capped at 1 MiB. Frozen upstream batch/streaming collectors have no comparable output cap and do not isolate a process group.

Frozen upstream streaming ignores provider timeout_ms and uses a fixed 10 second final wait with unbounded recording-stage pipe waits. Vinpst uses the same 10 second default when timeout_ms is absent, but an explicitly configured timeout bounds each streaming pipe write and final wait without imposing one whole-session deadline, so long recordings are not killed merely because their duration exceeds the provider timeout.

Existing Vinpst batch/JSON one-shot semantics intentionally keep timeout_ms=None as no configured deadline; managed provider materialization supplies 60000 ms. Frozen upstream leaves an omitted timeout at integer zero, which can immediately expire its batch helper deadline. This pre-existing safer behavior is preserved rather than copying the zero-timeout edge case.

The former one-shot LegacyCommandStreamingRunner is now test-only protocol coverage; production factory wiring uses LegacyCommandStreamingBackend. The .streaming suffix remains the authoritative selector and registry validation already requires stream metadata to agree with that suffix.
Live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification is now completed by the separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit; this command unit continues to own helper protocol/process semantics only.

audits.title: Native Sherpa offline and streaming recognition runtime
notes: Fixed native PCM scaling to divide signed i16 samples by 32768.0 for both offline and online recognizers, matching frozen upstream full-scale normalization.

Fixed native session lifecycle parity: repeated Finish is idempotent, Cancel is idempotent and yields Completed, and a completed recognizer with no text is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend error.
Restored upstream result extraction fallback: non-empty result.text wins; otherwise concatenated result.tokens are trimmed and used for offline results, online partials/endpoints, and final results.

Fixed online endpoint behavior: after each decode step, endpoint detection emits any changed hypothesis before resetting the stream, then decoding continues. Endpoint reset does not invent an application-level final/commit; push-to-talk still finalizes on StopRecording.
Fixed stop-time online projection so a final hypothesis that differs from the last emitted partial is first emitted as PartialText and then FinalText, exactly matching frozen upstream.

Model hotwords are now gated by top-level supports_hotwords. Provider hotwords override model hotwords, unsupported models ignore them at runtime, and an effective hotword path forces modified_beam_search for both offline and online recognizers.

Added all frozen-upstream online families supported by the sherpa-onnx Rust binding: transducer, zipformer2_ctc, paraformer, nemo_ctc, and t_one_ctc, with path-level metadata tests and native-feature compilation.

Aligned thread policy: offline metadata defaults to 4 threads when omitted while explicit offline model metadata may override it; online runtime uses the frozen upstream runtime default of 4 threads rather than model metadata.
All frozen offline family mappings are now owned and completed by ASR-MODEL-001; this runtime unit retains only recognizer/session behavior ownership.

Known gap: frozen upstream can supply model tokens and hotwords through in-memory tokens_buf/hotwords_buf JSON byte strings. The later model-manager audit verified that sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe high-level OfflineModelConfig/OnlineModelConfig does not expose those C-API fields, so Vinpst keeps the gap explicit rather than adding raw unsafe FFI.
Model path discovery/layout inference and VAD remain supporting evidence only and stay pending for their own non-overlapping audits.

audits.title: Offline Silero VAD trimming
notes: Silero detector construction matches frozen upstream: 16 kHz, 512-sample window, threshold/min-speech/min-silence controls, max speech duration 0, one CPU thread, debug disabled, and a 30 second detector buffer.

VAD config defaults are exactly aligned at enabled=true, threshold=0.45, min_speech_duration=0.15, min_silence_duration=0.5, and speech_pad_ms=300; config-level and resolved-plan tests pin the mapping so the two duration fields cannot be swapped.

Trim behavior matches upstream for reset, exact 512-sample feeds, zero-padding the final partial window, flush, segment extraction, independent per-segment speech padding, concatenation including overlapping padded regions, and returning original audio when no speech is found.

VAD model resolution intentionally differs from the frozen compile-time VINPUT_VAD_MODEL_PATH: Vinpst supports an explicit VINPST_SHERPA_VAD_MODEL, user/system XDG data locations, and a development asset. Missing/unloadable VAD still fails open to untrimmed audio like upstream.

Vinpst intentionally adds a 500 ms cold-start guard for the first detected segment: if its padded start lies within the first 500 ms, trimming preserves audio from sample zero to reduce first-syllable clipping after capture startup. Frozen vad_trimmer.cpp has no equivalent guard.

Frozen upstream initializes the detector at 16 kHz and ignores the sample_rate argument passed to Trim. Vinpst production capture is likewise 16 kHz, but injected/non-16-kHz PCM explicitly bypasses VAD instead of running a 16-kHz detector against mismatched-rate samples.
VAD remains offline/buffered only in both implementations; online/streaming Sherpa recognition does not use this trimmer.

audits.title: Installed ASR model discovery, metadata, layout, and removal
notes: Audited frozen installed-model discovery, metadata/path validation, runtime-language hints, model validation/removal safety, and native Sherpa family asset mapping without absorbing live registry network/schema ownership.

Fixed metadata path containment for offline and online Sherpa assets, including parent and symlink escapes; managed removal now rejects symlink targets and verifies canonical root containment while retaining Vinpst active-model protection.

Fixed native model coverage and metadata semantics: all 19 frozen offline families and all five frozen streaming families are accepted, including nemo_transducer family-keyed assets, Moonshine v2 encoder+merged-decoder layouts, frozen Qwen3/FunASR defaults, Whisper timestamp flags, and frozen RuntimeLanguageHint behavior.

Installed discovery now preserves malformed metadata entries as explicit broken models instead of failing the whole catalog; CLI reports broken state, daemon target menus exclude broken models, and GUI semantic state disables Use while keeping removal available.
Intentional Vinpst extensions remain: flat managed-model discovery in addition to the frozen two-level layout, a moonshine_v1 compatibility alias, and stronger active-model/symlink removal guards.

Remaining dependency gap: frozen tokens_buf/hotwords_buf in-memory Sherpa metadata cannot be represented through sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe Rust Offline/Online model configs; normal crates remain unsafe-free rather than bypassing the binding with raw FFI.

audits.title: Daemon error classification and notification payloads
notes: Ported the frozen daemon ClassifyErrorText taxonomy into one crate-private classifier preserving code, subject, detail, raw-message, prefix recursion, nested provider/model adoption, model/audio/D-Bus failures, LLM/HTTP processing failures, prompt-file URI parsing, and unknown fallback.

D-Bus emission now uses the classifier for recording-start failures, live streaming RecognitionEvent::Error, stop-time ASR failures, text postprocess failures, and current-generation ASR reload failures. Live Error events are drained in event order while the session retains its fatal state, so Stop produces no fabricated text and does not duplicate an already-emitted notification.

Private-session D-Bus evidence proves exact daemon_busy and asr_provider_timeout ssss payloads, live notification before Stop, stop-time notification before the operation failure, and bounded no-duplicate behavior. The complete daemon lib suite and 19 private-bus integration tests pass under strict dbus-integration Clippy.

The frozen header also defines daemon_start_failed and daemon_restart_failed, but frozen generation occurs only in cli/runtime/systemd_client.{cpp,h}, not error_info.cpp. The corresponding Rust CLI daemon-control files remain pending and do not yet project those two structured codes; that cross-module gap stays assigned to the later CLI-service audit rather than creating unused daemon constants.

audits.title: Legacy D-Bus names, status values, and ASR backend state classification
notes: Audited the frozen daemon service/notifier names, five wire status values, OperationFailed class, eight-field AsrBackendState shape, and requested-backend classification. The eight frozen daemon service methods and four signals remain present with the same member names; Notify is correctly kept on the separate frontend-notifier interface rather than the daemon service list.
Vinpst intentionally applies its independent product namespace to bus/object/interface/error/notifier identities and exposes additional daemon extension methods. No Vinput aliases are added.

Added ServiceStatus::parse_legacy_wire to reproduce frozen StringToStatus unknown->idle behavior while preserving the existing strict parse_wire API for Rust consumers so protocol drift remains fail-closed internally.

Requested ASR backend classification matches frozen precedence and exact provider/model equality. The eight state fields also match. Runtime projection intentionally differs for command/remote providers: Vinpst reports the model on the actual target/effective provider, while frozen ResolvePreferredLocalModel can report an unrelated active/first local model; the richer Vinpst diagnostic is retained.

Remote endpoints remain part of the frozen AsrBackendState shape. Vinpst fills them from the selected remote provider with diagnostic URL redaction; this is compatible with the field contract and more explicit than an empty-only projection.

audits.title: Daemon D-Bus method dispatch and signal emission
notes: Audited all eight frozen method handlers and four daemon signals against the Rust service facade. Legacy methods dispatch to the corresponding runtime or adapter operation and failures retain the Vinpst OperationFailed error class; runtime/controller state-machine semantics remain owned by later non-overlapping units.

Vinpst intentionally serializes recording transactions and completes inference/postprocessing before StopRecording returns the finalized JSON payload. Frozen upstream accepts StopRecording, returns an empty string immediately, and delivers the eventual result only by signal. The synchronous Rust contract is documented architecture, prevents stop/start overlap, and is consumed by the retained Rust Fcitx/CLI clients.

Session-bus ownership intentionally differs: frozen upstream requests replace-existing/allow-replacement, while Vinpst uses DoNotQueue so a second daemon cannot replace or queue behind the current owner. Private session-bus coverage pins the single-owner behavior.

Vinpst intentionally normalizes, credential-redacts, and bounds OperationFailed descriptions before exposing runtime errors on D-Bus instead of forwarding the frozen raw message verbatim. Focused coverage pins Authorization/Bearer redaction, whitespace normalization, and the Unicode-safe 512-character bound.

Frozen worker-thread signal forwarding uses an eventfd-backed queue into the bus thread. Rust uses zbus async signal emission from serialized service/runtime transitions and a generation-cancelled live-partial poller; private-bus integration coverage exercises recognition result/partial, status, notification, adapter, and reload paths without retaining the C++ queue mechanism.

Service lifetime is expressed through the held zbus Connection and Rust ownership rather than explicit Start/Stop bus methods: RuntimeState Drop restores output state, cancels capture/active recognition, and stops managed adapters, while the daemon explicitly shuts down its remote text service before releasing the service.

audits.title: Recognition result post-processing dispatch and status transition
notes: Fixed a user-visible status gap in the Rust-fused stop pipeline: non-empty recognized text no longer implies Postprocessing. Text-processor invocation and the postprocessing status transition are now separate decisions, matching the frozen recognition pipeline.

Normal scenes enter Postprocessing only when recognized text is non-empty, candidate_count is positive, provider_id is non-empty, and prompt is non-empty. Command scenes use the frozen command rule: recognized text, positive candidate_count, and a non-empty provider are sufficient; the command prompt is not an additional status gate.

Raw scenes, command paths without a configured processor provider, and adapter/no-provider scenes remain Inferring while the typed text processor still constructs the final payload. Focused runtime coverage and the private session-bus suite pin those negative cases, while a provider+prompt+candidate LLM scene pins the positive recording -> inferring -> postprocessing -> idle sequence.

Empty recognition already follows the frozen early-return behavior under ASR-CONTRACT-001. Final payload construction and text-provider/adapter semantics remain owned by the existing TXT-* units, while structured notification classification remains owned by ERROR-INFO-001.

Frozen RecognitionPipeline can report a null PostProcessor as a runtime error. Rust intentionally makes that state unrepresentable: RuntimeState owns a Box<dyn TextProcessor> at construction, so recognition cannot enter the pipeline without a processor object.

Frozen debug mode logs recognized text, truncated after 2048 bytes. Vinpst intentionally does not copy that diagnostic because its architecture contract forbids structured tracing from including recognized text; timing and target metadata remain sufficient for runtime diagnostics without retaining user dictation content.
The controller's worker scheduling, capture lifetime, status callbacks, and stop/reload state-machine ownership remain pending in DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001 and are not duplicated here.

audits.title: Daemon recording controller state machine and active-session orchestration
notes: Fixed controller-level buffered preprocessing to follow the frozen audio algebra instead of the earlier generic Rust helper: fixed silence-threshold trimming is no longer injected at this layer, i16 gain uses clamp plus truncation toward zero, and normalize_audio only amplifies a non-silent peak below 0.1 to full scale without attenuating louder audio. Silero VAD remains owned by ASR-VAD-001 rather than being duplicated in the controller.

Vinpst intentionally applies configured input_gain to both buffered and streaming sessions. Frozen streaming delivery applies the gain, but frozen buffered StopRecording overwrites its gain-adjusted callback buffer with raw StopAndGetBuffer PCM before inference and therefore drops the gain. That contradicts the frozen GUI/config contract describing input gain as a microphone multiplier applied to captured audio; Vinpst retains the user-facing contract rather than reproducing that upstream buffered-path bug.

Fixed live streaming PushAudio failures to become observable immediately instead of being deferred until StopRecording: the next live poll enters Error, disables capture callbacks, cancels the active recognition session/capture, restores output, emits error status plus the raw daemon notification, then recovers to Idle. Runtime and private-session D-Bus coverage prove this path without requiring a StopRecording call. RecognitionEvent::Error remains the separate frozen behavior owned by ERROR-INFO-001: it emits a classified notification while recording and is not promoted to the controller Error phase.

Start/rollback ordering is aligned and pinned: capture begins before RecognitionSession creation; session-creation failure cancels already-started capture and returns Idle; successful setup then exposes Recording and output ducking. Rust additionally gates early recorder callbacks until the session is installed and replays them in order, avoiding a frozen-style start-window race without changing delivered PCM order.

Streaming delivery matches the frozen controller's 800-sample chunk size, applies gain before each push, and flushes one final short tail without replaying already-delivered samples. Buffered and streaming paths both retain the frozen 8000 raw-sample minimum recording gate before ASR finishing.

Stop/reload/shutdown ownership is intentionally split rather than duplicated: Vinpst's serialized synchronous StopRecording transaction is recorded under DBUS-SERVICE-001, backend preparation/generation semantics under ASR-SESSION-001, and output-ducker/capture internals remain pending dedicated audio units. Reset-to-idle still applies a deferred reload, and RuntimeState Drop disables callbacks, cancels active recognition/capture, restores output, and cleans up supervised adapters.

Frozen eventfd notification, deferred capture-stop queue, start_recording_in_progress flag, and native worker thread primarily serialize races created by its callback/thread model. Vinpst intentionally uses the D-Bus recording transaction lock, Rust ownership/RAII, the capture-start gate, and async task cancellation instead of recreating those mechanisms. The frozen timing-only debug markers for recording start, first non-silent chunk, and first partial are not required product behavior and are not copied into user-content-safe tracing.

Recognition postprocessing remains owned by RECOGNITION-PIPELINE-001; audio capture implementation and output-ducker internals remain separate pending units, so this controller audit does not claim those files by supporting reference.

audits.title: Default output sink ducking and restoration
notes: Audited frozen wpctl behavior end to end: both implementations use @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@, a 2000 ms command deadline, current_volume * clamped_scale, four-decimal set-volume arguments, successful-set-before-saving semantics, idempotent repeated Duck, and one-shot Restore that clears saved state even if restoration fails.

Fixed a Rust process-supervision gap by replacing the output-ducker's private poll/spawn/read loop with the shared vinpst-process supervisor. The deadline now covers output recovery, stdout/stderr are bounded, and the direct child plus inherited descendants are reaped as one process group. Focused coverage proves both an ordinary timeout and the former parent-exit/descendant-held-output-pipe hang case.

Vinpst intentionally parses wpctl output more strictly than frozen strtod: non-finite and negative volumes are rejected, and the numeric token must parse completely. set-volume likewise rejects non-finite/negative values. Normal plain and [MUTED] wpctl output remains compatible; the stricter behavior is fail-closed for malformed external output.

Frozen OutputDucker uses an internal mutex because it may be called across its native controller threads. Rust requires mutable ownership of OutputDucker and serializes controller transitions instead, so reproducing the mutex would add no product behavior. Logging is routed through tracing rather than frozen stderr/debug helpers.

Controller-level duck/restore call ordering and shutdown restoration are already owned and covered by DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001; this unit only owns the volume-control implementation and process boundary.

audits.title: PipeWire capture lifecycle, target binding, and reusable stream policy
notes: Aligned the live PipeWire stream contract with frozen AudioCapture: S16LE at 16 kHz mono, Audio/Capture/Communication properties, stream.capture.sink=false so autoconnect targets sources rather than sink output, optional target.object for explicit sources, and AUTOCONNECT|INACTIVE|MAP_BUFFERS stream flags.

Removed Vinpst's extra RT_PROCESS request. The frozen capture stream does not request realtime process callbacks, while the Rust process path allocates a chunk Vec, extends the accumulated buffer, locks the callback holder, and may invoke a user callback; advertising that callback as RT-process-safe was both unnecessary for parity and a poor fit for its actual work.

Fixed reusable-stream fallback cleanup: when set_active(true) fails on a reused stream, Rust now drops the failed stream before creating the replacement, matching frozen DestroyStream-before-recreate semantics. A failed replacement therefore cannot leave the known-bad stream cached for another retry.

Reusable stream policy otherwise matches: reuse defaults on, explicit false-like opt-outs disable it, idle destroy defaults to 15000 ms and caps at 600000 ms, target/PCM mismatch forces recreation, successful stop deactivates and preserves the stream, and failed deactivation destroys it. Rust uses a generation-guarded timer worker instead of frozen daemon-main-loop polling for idle expiration; stale timers cannot destroy a new recording.

PCM delivery matches the frozen process callback: malformed/empty buffers are ignored, byte bounds are checked, odd trailing bytes are ignored, every accepted i16 sample is appended to the stop buffer and also forwarded to the installed chunk callback, and first-buffer latency is recorded once per recording. Rust copies PipeWire bytes into owned little-endian samples before callback delivery instead of exposing the mapped PipeWire buffer span directly.

Stop/cancel/drop semantics are equivalent at the product boundary: normal stop returns accumulated audio and either leaves a bounded inactive reusable stream or tears the worker down; cancellation discards the recording and destroys reusable state; Drop shuts down the worker and stream. Rust's dedicated worker owns its PipeWire main loop/context, whereas frozen AudioCapture keeps one pw_thread_loop for object lifetime.

Vinpst intentionally keeps independent environment names (VINPST_CAPTURE_REUSE / VINPST_CAPTURE_IDLE_DESTROY_MS), stream/client identity, and typed capture targets. Empty capture targets are rejected by typed config instead of being a second spelling of frozen default; the canonical user value is default. Idle target changes are lazily invalidated at the next Begin through config mismatch rather than immediately destroying the inactive stream, but the next recording cannot reuse the old target.

Frozen onParamChanged only prints the negotiated format; it does not reject a negotiated mismatch. Vinpst does not reproduce that stderr-only diagnostic. Device discovery code shares the Rust source file but remains pending for the separate common/audio/pipewire_device audit, and controller preprocessing/call ordering remains owned by DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001.

audits.title: PipeWire audio-source discovery and enumeration failure semantics
notes: Frozen and Rust discovery agree on the core registry contract: only PipeWire Node globals with media.class=Audio/Source are returned, registry arrival order is preserved, the registry object id is retained, and missing node.name/node.description values become empty strings. A direct run of both compiled CLIs against the live user PipeWire session returned the same two sources in the same 69 -> 55 order.

The one-shot synchronization model is equivalent: both attach the registry listener before issuing a core sync and stop the main loop only when the matching core done sequence arrives. Rust relies on pipewire-rs RAII for registry/core/context/main-loop cleanup instead of explicit destroy/disconnect calls.

Vinpst intentionally does not reproduce frozen failure ambiguity. Frozen EnumerateAudioSources returns an empty vector for main-loop/context/core setup failure, so its CLI cannot distinguish no microphones from PipeWire being unavailable. Rust returns AudioError::DeviceEnumerationFailed; CLI/daemon diagnostics degrade that to devices=[] plus live=false and enumeration_error while still exiting successfully, and the GUI surfaces a retryable microphone-refresh failure. Direct compiled-binary comparison with PIPEWIRE_REMOTE pointing at a missing server confirms this distinction.

Vinpst also keeps process-global pipewire-rs initialization instead of frozen per-call pw_init/pw_deinit. pipewire-rs guards pw_init with OnceLock, avoiding repeated global initialization/deinitialization when CLI/GUI discovery is invoked more than once or from independent product surfaces.

The Rust text device list deliberately retains the canonical default capture target even when live discovery fails, whereas frozen device list exits after its ambiguous empty-result message before printing default. This is consistent with Vinpst typed config: default remains a valid selection independent of whether live enumeration is currently available.

The shared Rust implementation file remains owned by AUDIO-CAPTURE-001 and is supporting evidence here. Device-list/use CLI command semantics beyond enumeration, and standalone-GUI presentation behavior beyond consuming the enumerator result, remain owned by their pending CLI/GUI audit units.

audits.title: Audio gain and quiet peak-normalization algebra
notes: Fixed the shared Rust i16 gain helper to match frozen ApplyGainI16 exactly at the sample boundary: multiply in f32, clamp to [-32768, 32767], then truncate toward zero. The previous generic helper rounded first, which could differ by one LSB; daemon buffered and streaming delivery now delegate to the corrected vinpst-audio implementation instead of maintaining duplicate controller math.

Moved frozen default PeakNormalize algebra into PcmBuffer::normalize_quiet_to_full_scale and made the controller delegate to it. Non-zero peaks below 0.1 full scale are amplified to full scale, peaks at or above the threshold are never attenuated, and zero audio is unchanged. Deterministic tests cover quiet/loud/silent cases and the exact i16 threshold boundary where 3276 is below 0.1 but 3277 is above it.

Removed the pre-parity AudioProcessingOptions abstraction plus its generic target-normalization and fixed-threshold silence-trimming helpers. Repository-wide search found no production consumer; the abstraction encoded the obsolete trim -> normalize -> gain order and its architecture documentation contradicted the audited runtime contract. Silence trimming remains owned by the separate Silero VAD backend rather than a fixed PCM threshold.

Updated the audio architecture contract to the actual product path: input gain is applied at capture delivery, buffered sessions optionally perform quiet-only peak normalization after gain, and this layer performs no fixed-threshold trim. Earlier prose claiming trim/normalize/gain was the buffered backend contract was stale scaffold documentation.

Frozen ApplyGain(float) has no caller and Rust has no product float-PCM processing surface, so Vinpst intentionally does not reproduce that dead generic helper. Frozen PeakNormalize's custom target_peak/low_threshold parameters are likewise unused; Rust exposes only the default production behavior instead of widening the public API for unexercised knobs.

Vinpst keeps its existing fail-closed handling for non-finite gain values: PcmBuffer leaves audio unchanged, while typed configuration rejects non-finite/out-of-range input_gain before runtime. Frozen product configuration also constrains gain, so this hardening does not change valid user behavior. The separate buffered-input-gain divergence caused by frozen StopAndGetBuffer overwrite remains documented under DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001.

audits.title: Remote browser text and Realtime-compatible service lifecycle
notes: Audited the full frozen service surface: remote-provider activation, 8080/1500 defaults, explicit/URL-derived port resolution, required trimmed API key, all-interface production bind, sorted non-loopback IPv4 endpoint discovery, single browser/input and Realtime/output ownership, debounce/finalize transitions, session.update echo, empty commit, and the committed -> transcription delta -> transcription completed sequence with one shared item id all match the Rust protocol/runtime behavior.

Fixed a lifecycle/security gap in the Axum rewrite. Frozen Shutdown explicitly shuts down every accepted/input/output fd before joining its threads; Rust previously stopped only the HTTP listener, so already-upgraded authenticated WebSockets survived provider disable, server shutdown, and API-key rotation on stale RemoteServerState. RemoteTextServer now broadcasts shutdown to input/output/debounce tasks before listener shutdown. Real socket tests prove both client classes close promptly and same-port API-key rotation evicts an old authenticated client before accepting only the new key.

Fixed browser-page functional parity without copying frozen presentation styling: a key entered through the prompt is now persisted to localStorage like the frozen page, reconnect resets both input/output status plus editor/count state, WebSocket errors close into the reconnect path, and the editor receives focus when both clients are ready. The simpler Vinpst visual treatment remains intentional product presentation rather than daemon-protocol behavior.

Aligned VINPST_ASR_DEBOUNCE_MS validation with frozen ParsePositiveInt's 32-bit signed-int range. 2147483647 ms is accepted and 2147483648 is rejected; the runtime field remains u64 so scheduling code does not need a narrower representation.

Aligned the frozen 2 MiB WebSocket frame resource boundary on both /ws and /v1/realtime by setting max_frame_size as well as max_message_size. Rust intentionally remains stricter for fragmented traffic because Tungstenite also caps the aggregate reassembled message at 2 MiB, while frozen only checks each raw frame independently. An integration test sends a 2 MiB + 1 frame and proves the connection is closed.

Authentication semantics match: browser auth uses the first {type:auth,api_key} message, Realtime is loopback-only with an exact Bearer key, and equal-length API-key comparison XOR-folds without an early mismatching-byte exit. Rust additionally redacts the key from Debug/status surfaces and uses standards-compliant Axum/Tungstenite WebSocket handshake, masking, fragmentation, ping/pong, and UTF-8 validation instead of reproducing frozen raw-parser permissiveness.

HTTP routing intentionally uses an explicit Axum route set: /, /health, /favicon.svg, /ws, and /v1/realtime. Frozen serves the editor for every otherwise-unknown GET; Rust returns normal 404 for unknown paths because the editor is not an SPA and no product flow depends on catch-all routing. Hyper's bounded HTTP/1 parser also has a larger framework buffer budget than frozen's exact 64 KiB aggregate-header limit; reproducing that smaller constant would require replacing the compact Axum serve boundary with custom connection plumbing, so the bounded framework behavior is retained and documented.

Rust intentionally uses deterministic monotonic event/item ids inside the protocol core instead of frozen wall-clock nanosecond ids. The ids remain opaque at the protocol boundary, every emitted event has the required prefix/uniqueness, and committed/delta/completed events share one item id as frozen clients require. Malformed or wrong-typed JSON is handled more defensively than frozen nlohmann value conversions and does not crash the service.

Namespace differences are deliberate project identity changes: provider.vinpst.remote.streaming and VINPST_ASR_* replace frozen provider.vinput.remote.streaming and VINPUT_ASR_*. RemoteTextLifecycle's async task/watch architecture replaces frozen accept/client/debounce native threads while preserving stop-before-rebind behavior; replacement bind failure leaves no stale listener, clients, or credentials.

audits.title: Daemon process startup, signal wait, and shutdown orchestration
notes: Fixed optional remote-service startup to match frozen degraded behavior. Frozen main logs a Synchronize failure and keeps the core D-Bus daemon running; Rust previously propagated start_remote_text_service and exited. Vinpst now reports `remote text service disabled (...)` to stderr, keeps the configured remote ASR target visible, exposes remote_text.running=false, and remains reachable for status/config repair.

Fixed startup ordering so the well-known D-Bus name is acquired before the optional remote listener starts, matching frozen dbus.Start-before-remote Synchronize ordering. This prevents a losing second daemon from briefly binding a remote port or accepting clients before DoNotQueue ownership fails. The expanded private-bus process smoke proves both occupied-port degraded startup and zero remote-listener side effects from a second owner candidate.

SIGINT and SIGTERM retain the frozen stop semantics through Tokio signal handling rather than an async-signal global flag. The process lifecycle smoke now uses SIGINT on the normal remote path and SIGTERM on degraded/owner paths, and verifies the remote listener disappears before process exit. Vinpst additionally supports an opt-in installed-executable inode replacement watcher; this is a documented package-upgrade supervision contract, not upstream parity surface, and exits unsuccessfully only when the package/activation profile enables it.

Configured ASR initialization remains intentionally fail-soft like frozen main: a normal configured D-Bus daemon installs an unavailable backend when preparation fails, remains idle/reloadable, and surfaces the startup error; strict one-shot commands still return the construction error. This behavior is separately proven by run-daemon-unavailable-asr-smoke.sh and owned in detail by the ASR/runtime audit units.

PipeWire startup is an intentional Rust resiliency divergence. Frozen main eagerly starts AudioCapture and treats capture startup failure as fatal; Vinpst constructs a lightweight PipeWireAudioRecorder and creates/connects its PipeWire stream only at BeginRecording. A temporarily absent PipeWire server therefore does not prevent D-Bus ownership or configuration repair, while the recording request returns the typed capture error. AUDIO-CAPTURE-001 owns the stream lifecycle details.

Config discovery keeps Vinpst's independent XDG/schema contract: explicit --config wins, otherwise the Vinpst user config is used and only an absent file falls back to the bundled default. Existing malformed/future-schema configs fail closed instead of frozen LoadCoreConfig's partial-default recovery. This is an established user-data protection policy in config-contract.md, not a main-loop parity gap.

Frozen's manual poll loop over D-Bus notification/runtime fds plus the one-second MaybeDestroyExpiredStream tick is replaced by zbus/Tokio tasks and component-owned wakeups/timers. PipeWire idle expiration is generation-guarded inside AUDIO-CAPTURE-001, while D-Bus/runtime workers own their asynchronous progress; main therefore does not reproduce a polling coordinator solely for structural similarity.

Top-level cleanup is equivalent through explicit remote shutdown plus Rust ownership. RuntimeState::Drop restores output ducking, removes the audio callback, cancels the active ASR session and capture, and stops supervised adapters; recorder/backend/process destructors then release their remaining resources. This replaces frozen's explicit postprocessor/remote/controller/recognition/adapter Shutdown sequence and releases the zbus connection before runtime teardown so no new service call can race cleanup.

The audit deliberately does not claim the AdapterSupervisor implementation embedded in frozen main.cpp: adapter process supervision remains owned by pending Rust adapter-process units. Likewise controller, D-Bus service, remote protocol, capture, and ASR internals are referenced only for startup/shutdown evidence and retain their dedicated audit ownership.

audits.title: Fcitx frontend D-Bus transport, daemon reconciliation, and signal delivery
notes: Fixed the frontend method deadline from the rewrite's former 60 seconds to the frozen five-second D-Bus deadline. The same five-second boundary now applies to the retained Fcitx event-loop Start/Stop calls and the safe Rust blocking status/menu client. The other runtime_defaults values are also preserved exactly: daemon failure cooldown 1500 ms, information notification timeout 3000 ms, and warning/error notification timeout 5000 ms.

Restored frozen responsiveness for StartRecording, StartCommandRecording, and StopRecording. They are dispatched with Fcitx callAsync instead of blocking zbus on the Fcitx thread. Rust still owns operation selection, active-scene/selected-text arguments, frontend session state, and response projection through a narrow prepare/pending/complete FFI seam; C++ owns only the mechanical Fcitx event-loop call required by the toolkit boundary.

Start sequencing now matches frozen behavior: once callAsync is successfully queued, the Rust frontend state is completed immediately into Recording/Commanding preedit. The later Start reply only clears or activates transport health/cooldown state and never consumes a subsequently prepared Stop call. This removes the rewrite race where a fast key release could prepare Stop before a late Start reply arrived.

Restored RecognitionResult as the final-result signal path. The retained Fcitx signal monitor now subscribes to RecognitionResult beside RecognitionPartial, StatusChanged, DaemonNotification, and owner changes. Rust now has a dedicated complete_recognition_result boundary independent of any pending Stop call, so both locally stopped and externally stopped sessions share the frozen final-signal semantics; the asynchronous Stop reply is only a transport-success/failure boundary and ASR/text postprocessing cannot block the Fcitx event loop.

Preserved frozen pending-call lifetime ordering. Start and Stop own independent Fcitx D-Bus slots, and frontend session reset no longer destroys either slot. Each callback reclaims its own slot, which is required when RecognitionResult and idle StatusChanged arrive before the Stop method reply. A native InputContext smoke schedules a timer 10 ms after Stop dispatch and requires it to fire before the final result, directly proving event-loop responsiveness.

Restored the frozen 1.5-second daemon-sync cooldown across session-bus connection failure, blocking status/menu RPC failure, scene/ASR selection failure, and asynchronous Start/Stop transport failure. A successful call or service-owner recovery clears the cooldown. Current error strings remain typed/localized at the Rust/frontend boundary rather than reproducing frozen ad-hoc reply-name formatting byte-for-byte.

Frozen queryAsrBackendState and restartDaemon have no callers in the frozen tree and are not reproduced as dead frontend interfaces. Frozen ASR menu selection persisted config and then separately called ReloadAsrBackend; current SetActiveAsrTarget performs validated selection, optional atomic persistence, and reload queueing as one typed daemon operation while preserving the same visible switch-request and failure behavior.

Current frontend reconciliation intentionally remains signal-driven rather than reproducing frozen ensureStatusSync's one-second blocking GetStatus poll. Like frozen rememberInputContext, every key event records the latest live Fcitx InputContext through a TrackableObjectReference. An unsolicited external recording/inferring/postprocessing status automatically adopts a normal Rust frontend session on that remembered context, so subsequent partial/result signals are displayed and committed without a Vinpst trigger. The monitor also samples the initial owner and performs an explicit bounded GetStatus before each local start; avoiding periodic blocking RPC keeps the Fcitx loop responsive without losing current-daemon transitions.

The full upstream file audit also covers preedit/status projection and notification handling. Current live-status state preserves partial-over-status priority, owner-loss reset, error-like notification reset, and information-notification non-interruption; notification icons and 3/5-second timeouts match frozen behavior. Vinpst namespace/app-name changes remain intentional independent-product identity changes.

The private-session async addon smoke uses a fresh daemon per frontend fixture and condition-driven Fcitx time events rather than fixed timing or mock-audio reuse, and passes three consecutive runs. Native InputContext evidence separately proves normal and command async paths plus a no-trigger external-session case: an independent client starts recording, the addon automatically renders the live partial on the remembered context, and the independent stop produces the final commit. The deterministic FFI ABI gate reports 65 public declarations matching archive symbols, the complete Fcitx CTest suite passes 11/11, and focused Rust frontend/core/transport tests pass 53/3/27 with strict Clippy. A cached real online-transducer gate could not run in this workspace because the raw model cache lacks the required vinpst-model.json typed metadata.

audits.title: Fcitx frontend notifier D-Bus ingress object
notes: Restored the frozen four-string notifier ingress contract as a thin Fcitx ObjectVTable method. The object accepts Notify(code, subject, detail, raw_message), has no output payload, and forwards the four values without reinterpretation before presentation planning.

Vinpst intentionally uses its independent frontend namespace: org.fcitx.Fcitx5.Vinpst1 at /org/fcitx/Fcitx5/Vinpst instead of the frozen Vinput interface/path. These values match the already-published vinpst-protocol frontend-notifier constants and do not add old-name aliases.

The normal addon registers the notifier object on the existing Fcitx D-Bus connection beside its signal monitor. Registration creates no extra bus, thread, or event loop; failure is a bounded warning and leaves the rest of the addon functional.

DaemonNotification signals and Notify method calls now share PlanStructuredDaemonNotification, which delegates severity/text selection to the existing Rust daemon-notification planner before using the same Fcitx presentation path. Raw/detail priority, localized unknown fallback, recording-reset policy, icons, and 3/5-second notification timeouts therefore cannot drift between the two ingress forms.

A private-session CTest owns org.fcitx.Fcitx5 on a receiver connection, registers the real object vtable, invokes Notify through a separate D-Bus sender, verifies all four strings and the empty method reply, then verifies the shared planner produces an error presentation with the expected raw text. The complete addon CTest suite passes 12/12.

This audit owns only the frontend receive object. Frozen cli/runtime/systemd_client.cpp is the live sender for daemon_start_failed/daemon_restart_failed and remains pending for the separate CLI service-control audit; restoring this ingress does not claim those current CLI failure paths already send Notify.

audits.title: Fcitx addon lifecycle, configuration, and recent-context capture
notes: Restored the frozen addon lifecycle boundaries without moving semantic state back into C++. InputContext key handling now runs at PreInputMethod as frozen upstream does. InputContext creation still requests SurroundingText and now immediately remembers the live TrackableObjectReference; destruction flushes only history owned by that context, while post-input-method CommitString events feed the Rust recent-context tracker. The dedicated addon factory remains a thin Fcitx construction boundary.

Fixed the previously disconnected recent-input writer. Rust now owns user-fragment buffering and persistence using the existing vinpst-text cache primitives: non-CJK fragments are space-joined, CJK boundaries remain tight, sentence-ending punctuation flushes immediately, input-context changes flush the previous buffer, ordinary fragments use the frozen five-second inactivity flush, and tracker drop performs final cleanup. File or config maintenance failure remains non-fatal to recognition.

Recognition history matches the frozen source policy. An explicit asr candidate is preferred; otherwise the first non-empty raw candidate is recorded as asr, with command mode excluding the original selected text captured by the Rust frontend session. A directly committed LLM result also records llm, candidate menus record the ASR side before display and add llm only when an LLM row is selected, and every generated non-cancel commit installs exact one-shot suppression so the following Fcitx CommitString event cannot duplicate it as user input.

The history tracker reads the canonical user JSON config on construction and frontend reload to compute the maximum scene.context_lines. It preserves the frozen every-100-writes truncation cadence when that maximum is nonzero while continuing to write history when it is zero, so later scene changes can consume existing context. The Fcitx INI remains intentionally limited to frontend trigger/mode settings; scene/provider ownership stays in the canonical daemon JSON config.

Deterministic evidence includes 56 vinpst-fcitx-core tests, 29 vinpst-fcitx-ffi tests, strict Clippy, 74 C ABI declarations matching the Rust archive, and the complete Fcitx CTest suite at 12/12. A private-session native InputContext run against the freshly rebuilt addon commits mock recognition result and leaves exactly one isolated JSONL row with source asr, proving RecognitionResult -> Rust presentation -> addon history -> disk without a duplicate user row.

One frozen sandbox lifecycle behavior remains open. Upstream addon startup automatically materializes and rewrites the user systemd service when running in a sandbox, then reloads the user manager. Current Flatpak packaging carries the unit and the typed CLI can explicitly render/install the host service, but the package smoke does not prove automatic first-use host installation after extension deployment. Reintroducing ad-hoc filesystem writes and system() calls in this thin addon would violate current ownership; this remains a service/sandbox audit gap rather than being hidden as an intentional divergence.

The monolithic addon/core/vinput.h declaration surface is closed separately by FCITX-HEADER-001 after the key-event and menu source units, so this core unit does not duplicate mixed declaration ownership. D-Bus transport/notifier behavior is already owned by FCITX-DBUS-001 and FCITX-NOTIFIER-001 and is supporting context here rather than duplicate ownership.

audits.title: Fcitx key-trigger routing, trigger timing, and selected-text input
notes: Trigger timing matches the frozen key-event path: 80 ms press debounce, 300 ms hold activation, and the 500 ms release/stop tail are Rust-owned together with Tap/Hold/Both state, modifier-release matching, pending-start cancellation, and active-recording stop decisions. The retained C++ adapter only schedules Fcitx native timers and reports semantic press/release events.

Fixed overlapping custom-trigger priority to the frozen order: ASR menu, then Scene menu, then normal dictation, then command dictation. This matters only when users intentionally assign the same key to multiple actions; ordinary disjoint configurations are unchanged. Result, Scene, and ASR visible-menu handling also retains the frozen result -> Scene -> ASR priority before voice triggers.

Fixed menu-trigger pass-through while a recording session is active. A Scene/ASR menu press rejected by Rust semantic gating is no longer unconditionally filterAndAccept'ed, so the application receives that press as frozen upstream does; the corresponding configured menu-key release remains consumed to avoid stray release delivery.

Restored keyboard control for the result candidate menu. The five-row result menu now handles configured PageUp/PageDown, digits, Up/Down, Enter/KP Enter, Escape, and matching releases with the frozen close/pass/consume behavior. Semantic action planning lives in Rust through the same menu-action ABI used by other menus; C++ only classifies Fcitx keys, reads toolkit cursor/page state, performs requested paging/cursor calls, and invokes the selected candidate.

Selected-text acquisition remains surrounding-text first with PRIMARY selection fallback and local rejection of an empty selection. The frozen command-start requirement for candidate_count > 0 plus an LLM provider is intentionally not restored: Vinpst supports command text adapters and a deterministic no-adapter raw/ASR candidate fallback, so command recording remains useful without an LLM provider. This is a product capability extension rather than an omitted gate.

Vinpst's current default keys intentionally remain Right Control for normal dictation and F10 for command mode, with Right Shift for Scene and F8 for ASR. These defaults have been the documented Vinpst product surface since the independent frontend rewrite; frozen Alt_R/Control_R defaults are not reintroduced here. Detailed Fcitx config-schema/default ownership remains assigned to the pending common/config/vinput_config audit.

Current Stop preserves the scene captured at recording start instead of reloading the active scene immediately before stop. This intentional typed-session behavior prevents a concurrent scene switch from changing postprocessing for an in-flight utterance; the transport and scene-capture contract is already covered by FCITX-DBUS-001.

Deterministic evidence includes 57 vinpst-fcitx-core tests, 30 vinpst-fcitx-ffi tests, strict Clippy, 75 public C ABI declarations matching archive symbols, focused key-trigger/result-menu/selection/trigger-mode smokes, and the complete Fcitx CTest suite at 12/12. The mixed addon/core/vinput.h declaration surface and broader menu implementation are owned by the later FCITX-HEADER-001 and FCITX-MENU-001 closeout units rather than being duplicated here.

audits.title: Fcitx Scene, ASR, and recognition-result menus
notes: Scene, ASR, and recognition-result menu semantics are fully split from the toolkit adapter. Rust owns filter/query state, UTF-8 editing, action priority, release handling, page targets, row filtering, current/effective summaries, target controls, result-candidate comments, preferred cursor policy, and selection semantics. Retained C++ owns Fcitx key classification, CommonCandidateList construction, cursor/page calls, gettext fragments, InputPanel publication, and execution of Rust-projected controls.

Fixed a main-loop responsiveness regression in the rewritten Scene and ASR menus. Menu activation no longer performs the bounded synchronous typed D-Bus refresh on the Fcitx event loop. A cached Rust snapshot is published immediately when available, while a fresh typed controller is loaded on a worker and moved back through Fcitx EventDispatcher. No D-Bus tuple decoding, registry parsing, or provider/config model was duplicated into C++.

Background refresh is generation- and lifetime-guarded. InputContext watch validity, addon lifetime, and a per-menu sequence are checked before publishing; closing, switching, selecting, or destroying the addon invalidates older work so an in-flight snapshot cannot overwrite a newer user choice. Refresh failure preserves an already-published cached menu and only presents daemon-unavailable feedback when no usable cached projection existed.

A dedicated private-bus responsiveness gate deliberately activates a service that sleeps without acquiring org.fcitx.Vinpst. Both Scene and ASR menu trigger calls return in under 100 ms while a 50 ms Fcitx event-loop probe still fires, proving blocked D-Bus activation is off the input loop. The ordinary private-bus daemon gate separately proves successful asynchronous publication into a native InputContext: Scene renders Current: Raw with selectable alternatives and ASR renders Current: mock-streaming.

The configured ASR menu lifecycle remains intact: the deterministic private-bus installed-model smoke passes target selection, persistence, loading/effective projection, and reload behavior. Result-menu construction and selection also match the frozen source through the Rust presentation/history contracts: five-row paging, source comments, preferred commit cursor, cancel behavior, command selection replacement, LLM history, and one-shot generated-commit suppression. Keyboard routing itself is already owned and tested by FCITX-INPUT-001.

Vinpst intentionally differs in configuration ownership. Frozen vinput_menu.cpp reads and writes scene/provider/model configuration and registry/model metadata directly in the addon; current menus consume daemon-owned typed Scene/ASR snapshots and mutate them through SetActiveScene and SetActiveAsrTarget. A cold menu with no cached projection therefore waits asynchronously for the daemon snapshot instead of reconstructing a second local config/registry view; transient refresh failure can keep an already-published cache. This keeps the Fcitx addon thin and gives CLI, GUI, remote, and Fcitx one canonical runtime/config authority rather than reintroducing a second frontend-side configuration model.

Deterministic evidence includes 57 vinpst-fcitx-core tests, 30 vinpst-fcitx-ffi tests, strict Clippy, 75 public C ABI declarations matching archive symbols, the complete Fcitx CTest suite at 12/12, the blocked-activation responsiveness smoke, the ordinary private-bus native menu publication probes, and the configured ASR installed-model target-switch smoke. The final mixed addon/core/vinput.h declaration ownership is closed by FCITX-HEADER-001 now that core, input, and menu implementation units are complete.

audits.title: Fcitx monolithic addon declaration closeout
notes: The frozen VinputEngine header is a monolithic declaration aggregator, not an additional behavior owner. Its constructor/factory, InputContext lifecycle, context-history, DBus/signal/notifier, key-trigger timing, Scene/ASR/result menus, and frontend result/session declarations map to the already-audited FCITX-CORE-001, FCITX-DBUS-001, FCITX-NOTIFIER-001, FCITX-INPUT-001, and FCITX-MENU-001 implementation units. Current headers are excluded from the current source inventory, so this closeout intentionally owns no synthetic current source file.

Frozen Session, menu visibility/filter vectors, active-scene/provider mirrors, partial text, selected command text, result candidate vectors, suppression text, and cached backend state are not reproduced as one mutable C++ object. Rust frontend, trigger, menu-controller, daemon-signal, presentation, and context-history owners hold those semantic states; retained C++ fields are limited to toolkit references, native timers/slots, typed RAII handles, and short-lived transport/menu-refresh bookkeeping.

Frozen restartDaemon and queryAsrBackendState declarations are intentionally absent because the frozen tree has no live caller for those interfaces and current backend switching/recovery is daemon-owned. Frozen periodic ensureStatusSync/stopStatusSync declarations are also not restored: service-owner signals plus bounded pre-start reconciliation provide the audited current behavior without a one-second blocking status poll.

The header-level trigger-key initializers are not treated as authoritative user defaults because frozen applySettings replaces them from VinputSettings. Vinpst frontend defaults and trigger-mode schema remain in fcitx_config and are audited separately against common/config/vinput_config; the documented Vinpst defaults therefore are not silently inferred from this frozen implementation-detail initializer.

The factory remains a dedicated thin Fcitx AddonFactory, while the large VinputEngine declaration is intentionally decomposed into focused C++ boundary headers and Rust semantic controllers. This is an architectural divergence that reduces duplicated mutable frontend state while preserving the behavior proven by the source-level units.

audits.title: Rust Fcitx crate roots and string FFI glue
notes: These files are rewrite-only glue with no frozen C++ source counterpart. The crate roots expose the already-audited Rust frontend modules without adding a second semantic implementation, and ffi_string.rs centralizes raw borrowed UTF-8 validation plus owned-string view/free mechanics used by the C ABI.

Keeping string borrowing and output construction in one Rust FFI module is intentional: retained C++ passes byte views and never reimplements UTF-8 validation or Rust allocation ownership. The public ABI gate currently proves 75 header declarations exactly match archive symbols, while strict Clippy and the FFI unit suite cover invalid/atomic input handling.
This current-only unit exists so the file-by-file ledger accounts for rewrite-specific source inventory explicitly rather than forcing glue files under unrelated frozen modules.

audits.title: Fcitx frontend trigger and menu configuration
notes: The retained frontend INI keeps the frozen seven behavioral fields and wire keys: TriggerMode, TriggerKey, CommandKeys, SceneMenuKey, AsrMenuKey, PagePrevKeys, and PageNextKeys. Key-list constraints still allow modifier-only, modifierless, and ordinary modified keys; Tap/Hold/Both values and PageUp/KP_PageUp/PageDown/KP_PageDown paging defaults remain aligned. Load falls back to typed defaults when fields are absent and the config object round-trips all seven settings.

Vinpst intentionally uses conf/vinpst.conf instead of conf/vinput.conf and documents Right Control for normal dictation plus F10 for command dictation, while retaining Right Shift for Scene, F8 for ASR, and Both trigger mode. These defaults are the established independent-product surface and are not reverted to the frozen Alt_R/Control_R pair. The frozen source also contains stale tooltip wording that disagrees with its own Scene key initializer, so those prose tooltips are not mechanically copied into the slimmer Vinpst config page.

Fixed a discoverability regression from the rewrite by restoring the frozen ExternalOption user task. VinpstFrontendConfig now exposes a ManagementGui external action that launches vinpst-gui from the Fcitx configuration UI; it uses Vinpst names instead of restoring the frozen ModelManager/vinput-gui identity. The zh_CN catalog includes the launcher label.

Current save behavior is intentionally safer than frozen safeSaveAsIni(config): it reads the existing RawConfig, overwrites only owned typed fields, and writes the merged tree. The config smoke proves unknown legacy/future keys survive a settings save instead of being discarded, while owned settings reload exactly.

Deterministic evidence includes the localized config smoke covering defaults, all trigger/menu/page fields, Hold round-trip, unknown-key preservation, TriggerMode enum/i18n metadata, and the External launcher type plus exact vinpst-gui URI. The complete Fcitx CTest suite passes 13/13 after rebuilding translations and the addon.

audits.title: Fcitx frontend gettext locale and domain handling
notes: Locale normalization and catalog discovery remain aligned with frozen common/i18n: LANGUAGE, LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG, and the active LC_MESSAGES locale are considered in order; encoding/modifier suffixes and LANGUAGE fallbacks are normalized; build-tree catalogs are preferred when present and installed catalogs remain the fallback.

Fixed a rewrite regression in locale-category selection. After setlocale(LC_ALL, ""), the frontend now restores the frozen preferred-message-locale behavior by trying the normalized LANGUAGE/LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG choice as bare, .UTF-8, and .utf8 LC_MESSAGES values. Before this fix, LANGUAGE=zh_CN with LC_ALL=C or C.UTF-8 incorrectly fell back to English even when the Chinese catalog existed.

Vinpst intentionally uses the fcitx5-vinpst translation domain and Fcitx registerDomain/translateDomain instead of changing the process-global gettext textdomain to fcitx5-vinput. This keeps the retained addon from taking global domain ownership inside the Fcitx process while preserving domain-local UTF-8 translations. VINPST_FCITX_LOCALEDIR is an additive deterministic-test/development override.

The current helper also owns formatted count/value/page translation wrappers so C++ call sites do not duplicate snprintf allocation logic. These helpers preserve translated formatting behavior without expanding semantic frontend state.

Deterministic evidence includes the existing localized message/format/fallback smoke plus a second invocation with LANGUAGE=zh_CN and LC_ALL=C. Both pass against the built zh_CN catalog, proving the frozen LANGUAGE override behavior while retaining Fcitx-native domain registration.

audits.title: CLI root parser, registration, and dispatch surface
notes: The frozen root registration surface is preserved under the Vinpst executable identity. init, model, provider, llm, adapter, hotword, device, scene, config, daemon, and recording are all registered as user commands; recording again exposes the frozen visible rec alias. Current doctor is an additive user-facing Vinpst diagnostic, while protocol, registry transport inspection, ASR state, raw audio-device, activation-service, mock-result, and status plumbing remain callable but hidden from ordinary root help.

Fixed root parser regressions introduced by the Clap rewrite. The root subcommand is optional again: invoking vinpst without arguments prints the generated root help to stdout and exits successfully. The version flag is again visible as -v,--version, while the previously generated Clap -V remains a hidden accepted short alias so pre-0.1 rewrite users are not broken. The generated program name is explicitly vinpst instead of leaking the Rust package name vinpst-cli into help/version output.

Global -j,--json remains available and current parsing intentionally accepts it both before and after subcommands, which is more permissive than the frozen CLI11 root option placement. Deep command JSON forcing is delegated through the typed Command enum instead of a shared mutable Formatter/CliAction closure; individual command output contracts remain owned by later CLI units.

The root dispatch architecture intentionally differs from frozen CliAction registration. CLI11 stores one std::function selected during registration; Clap parses a typed enum and main.rs dispatches it. This removes callback wiring without changing the user command selected. The config/control action headers are alias-only registration glue and are accounted here rather than treated as behavior modules.

Parser-library error exit codes are intentionally not normalized. Frozen CLI11 returns its library-specific code 109 for unknown commands/options, while Clap uses conventional CLI parse exit code 2; both fail before action dispatch and write the diagnostic to stderr. Help, version, no-argument help, and rec help all exit 0.

Deterministic evidence includes structural help-surface tests for the exact visible root command set, hidden maintenance commands/options, familiar upstream aliases, optional root subcommand, rec, the vinpst program identity, and -v metadata; process-level tests prove no-argument help exits 0 and both -v plus the hidden -V compatibility alias succeed. The complete vinpst-cli test suite and strict all-target Clippy pass.

audits.title: CLI first-run initialization workflow
notes: The frozen init user task remains intact: vinpst init creates the default per-user configuration and managed model directory, leaves an existing configuration untouched by default, is idempotent when everything already exists, and -f,--force replaces only the configuration with the bundled default. The rewrite had retained --force but lost the frozen -f short form; this audit restores it and pins the short form in the force integration test.

The init implementation is now isolated in commands/init.rs instead of sharing the 652-line commands/system.rs catch-all. The move is behavior-preserving and gives the frozen init_actions/register_init ownership a dedicated Rust module; system.rs is reduced to 402 lines and remains pending for its separate diagnostics/activation-service ownership.

Vinpst intentionally extends frozen init with --dry-run, --json, hidden deterministic --config/--model-root/--cache-root overrides, XDG-aware cache-root creation, activation-service planning metadata, and concise next-step guidance. These extensions do not change the default write contract and keep fixture/path controls out of ordinary help.

Default config creation is stricter than frozen InitializeCoreConfig: the bundled typed config is parsed and validated before writes, the destination is written atomically with private permissions, and the integration gate validates the produced config. Existing model/cache directories are never replaced by --force; only missing managed directories are created.

Deterministic evidence covers XDG default path planning without writes, creation of config/model/cache roots, 0600 config permissions on Unix, config validation, idempotent rerun without rewriting, preservation of an existing config without force, and replacement through the restored -f short flag. Focused init tests and strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy pass.

audits.title: CLI config get, set, and editor workflows
notes: The frozen config get/set/edit command family and g/s/e parser aliases remain available under Vinpst. Both implementations expose JSON-pointer get/set semantics; current get additionally supports existence checks and typed/default fallback output, while current set deliberately requires the pointer to already exist and a dry-run/output/in-place write decision instead of silently mutating the user config.

Fixed the rewrite loss of frozen config set -i,--stdin. VALUE is optional when --stdin is present, standard input lines are joined with newline separators using the frozen behavior, and the resolved multiline value then follows the same current parse/string override, whole-config validation, backup, and atomic-write pipeline as a positional value. An integration test pipes two lines into an existing scene prompt and verifies both JSON output and the persisted value.

Restored explicit config edit core|fcitx compatibility without giving up the safer Vinpst editor workflow. The target defaults to core for the existing Vinpst UX; core edits a temporary pretty JSON copy and must parse plus validate before replacement, while fcitx resolves the XDG Fcitx frontend file at fcitx5/conf/vinpst.conf and keeps the INI text opaque to the daemon schema. Both targets run the editor against a private temporary file, preserve an existing adjacent backup, and only then atomically replace the destination.

Frozen config edit invokes the editor directly on the live file and therefore offers no rollback or schema check. The current temporary-file, backup, and atomic-replace behavior is an intentional safety divergence. Core also supports --editor and VINPST_CONFIG_EDITOR before EDITOR/VISUAL, dry-run planning, and JSON diagnostics; fcitx rejects --config because that option names the core JSON source and should not ambiguously retarget the frontend INI.

Current validate is an additive user command and example remains hidden maintenance/export plumbing. Set adds --string, --output, --in-place, --dry-run, and JSON diagnostics; get adds --exists/--default. These extensions keep ordinary help task-oriented and do not remove the frozen get/set/edit tasks or aliases.

Deterministic evidence includes 22 config-mutation integration tests covering JSON-pointer reads, defaults/existence, multiline stdin, string coercion, validated dry-run/output/in-place mutation, invalid-update rejection, backups, core editor validation, invalid editor-output rollback, and XDG Fcitx INI editing with backup. Strict all-target vinpst-cli Clippy passes, and generated help shows config set <POINTER> [VALUE] with -i,--stdin plus config edit [TARGET] with core/fcitx choices.

audits.title: CLI ASR provider, model, and hotword workflows
